final_message:
I reproduced it, with no multidict needed. On PyPy, collecting a 138-item test file crashes with `INTERNALERROR> KeyError` in `reorder_items_atscope` (the `move_to_end(i, last=False)` call). It happens on every run with this checkout and with pytest 8.2.2. The same file collects fine on pytest 8.2.1 under PyPy and on CPython, which matches your 8.2.1/8.2.2 bisect.

Run from the repo root: `bash repro_13312/run.sh`. It needs network on first run: it downloads PyPy 3.10 v7.3.17 into `~/.cache/repro_13312`, or set `PYPY=/path/to/pypy3` to use your own. It exits 1 when the bug shows.

The patch adds four files:
- repro_13312/test_repro.py: a session fixture with one param, a module fixture with three params, and `parametrize("i", range(46))`. That gives 138 items, and they all go into one OrderedDict in `reorder_items`.
- repro_13312/od_only.py: the same `d[k] = None; d.move_to_end(k, last=False)` pattern on a plain `OrderedDict` of 126 ints, without pytest. On PyPy it raises `KeyError(125)` and leaves 127 entries, one key twice. That matches the duplicate keys you saw in pdb. CPython runs it without error.
- repro_13312/pytest.ini: keeps the repo's own config out of the run.
- repro_13312/run.sh: the runner.

**When it triggers:** across 1,440 generated test files, it failed only when one argkey's OrderedDict held about 126–170 items. Bigger or smaller files collect fine. That explains why your multidict test set broke only at certain sizes. Item hashes don't matter: the result was the same on every run despite PyPy's random hash seeds.

**Likely cause (an inference, not verified):** I think the bug is in PyPy's ordered dict, not in pytest's logic. In PyPy's `rordereddict.py`, `ll_dict_move_to_first` makes room at the front by growing the entries array, then rebuilds the index without enlarging it. A dict of up to 170 items uses a 256-slot index that stores one-byte positions. Once the entries array grows past about 254 slots, positions no longer fit in a byte, so lookups miss and `d[k] = None` adds a duplicate. 170 is two-thirds of 256, which fits the upper edge of the failing range. On the pytest side, this only became reachable because 8.2.2 started calling `move_to_end(..., last=False)`.

I tested only PyPy 3.10 v7.3.17, not the 3.9 or 3.11 builds from the report.
patch:
diff --git a/repro_13312/od_only.py b/repro_13312/od_only.py
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..9ec1796e
--- /dev/null
+++ b/repro_13312/od_only.py
@@ -0,0 +1,21 @@
+# Same pattern without pytest: reorder_items_atscope does
+#   d[i] = None; d.move_to_end(i, last=False)
+# for each block of items, in reverse order. On PyPy this raises KeyError (and
+# leaves duplicate keys in the OrderedDict); on CPython it finishes fine.
+import sys
+from collections import OrderedDict
+
+n, blocks = 126, 6
+d = OrderedDict.fromkeys(range(n))
+for g in range(blocks):
+    block = [k for idx, k in enumerate(list(d)) if idx * blocks // n == g]
+    for k in reversed(block):
+        d[k] = None
+        try:
+            d.move_to_end(k, last=False)
+        except KeyError:
+            keys = list(d)
+            print(f"{sys.implementation.name}: KeyError({k!r}) in move_to_end; "
+                  f"len(d)={len(d)}, iterated keys={len(keys)}, distinct={len(set(keys))}")
+            sys.exit(1)
+print(f"{sys.implementation.name}: OK, len(d)={len(d)}")
diff --git a/repro_13312/pytest.ini b/repro_13312/pytest.ini
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..eea2c180
--- /dev/null
+++ b/repro_13312/pytest.ini
@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+[pytest]
diff --git a/repro_13312/run.sh b/repro_13312/run.sh
new file mode 100755
index 00000000..cc4b4389
--- /dev/null
+++ b/repro_13312/run.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,31 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Usage: bash repro_13312/run.sh   (from repo root)
+# Uses $PYPY if set, otherwise downloads PyPy 3.10 v7.3.17 into ~/.cache/repro_13312.
+set -u
+HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
+REPO="$(cd "$HERE/.." && pwd)"
+CACHE="${HOME}/.cache/repro_13312"
+mkdir -p "$CACHE"
+if [ -z "${PYPY:-}" ]; then
+  PYPY="$CACHE/pypy3.10-v7.3.17-linux64/bin/pypy3"
+  if [ ! -x "$PYPY" ]; then
+    curl -sSL https://downloads.python.org/pypy/pypy3.10-v7.3.17-linux64.tar.bz2 | tar xj -C "$CACHE"
+  fi
+fi
+VENV="$CACHE/venv-pypy"
+if [ ! -x "$VENV/bin/python" ]; then
+  "$PYPY" -m venv "$VENV"
+  SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION=8.4.0.dev0 "$VENV/bin/pip" install -q -e "$REPO" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
+    || SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION=8.4.0.dev0 "$VENV/bin/pip" install -q -e "$REPO"
+fi
+"$VENV/bin/python" -VV | tail -1
+echo "== OrderedDict alone (PyPy):"
+PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 "$VENV/bin/python" "$HERE/od_only.py"
+echo "== pytest --collect-only (PyPy, this checkout):"
+cd "$HERE"
+out="$(PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 "$VENV/bin/python" -m pytest --collect-only -q -p no:cacheprovider test_repro.py 2>&1)"
+echo "$out" | grep -E "^INTERNALERROR>  +File .*fixtures.py|^INTERNALERROR> KeyError|tests? collected"
+if echo "$out" | grep -q "^INTERNALERROR> KeyError"; then
+  echo "BUG REPRODUCED"; exit 1
+fi
+echo "no KeyError"; exit 0
diff --git a/repro_13312/test_repro.py b/repro_13312/test_repro.py
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..635a5e4e
--- /dev/null
+++ b/repro_13312/test_repro.py
@@ -0,0 +1,21 @@
+# Reproducer: on PyPy, fixture reordering crashes collection with
+# INTERNALERROR KeyError in reorder_items_atscope (move_to_end).
+# All 3 x 46 = 138 items share the session-scoped argkey ("sess", 0), which puts
+# one OrderedDict in reorder_items in the failing size range (~126-170 items);
+# the module-scoped "mod" param then moves blocks of those items to the front.
+import pytest
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="session", params=["only"])
+def sess(request):
+    return request.param
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module", params=range(3))
+def mod(request):
+    return request.param
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("i", range(46))
+def test_it(sess, mod, i):
+    pass
